html:
Agent Checks and execution authority

Agent Checks are the named guard definitions in runtime_guard_policy.py. Categories include completion/evidence, mutation/execution, environment/target, routing, resource limits and recovery/convergence. Each definition records its enforcement owner, resume strategy and bypass meaning. The resolver combines accepted snapshots with versioned run overrides; the algorithm being controlled stays with its subsystem.

Guard settings merge per check, in Global, Conversation, Prompt, then Run order; this differs from the complete-snapshot replacement used by capability and permission policies. Explicit edits require registered IDs and strict booleans. Accepted runs restore their saved values and source map rather than adopting later global defaults. Unknown checks resolve as unavailable. During an active Web Research task, disabling Research proof also disables its dependent structure, citation, receipt and complete- observation checks in the resolver; the reported source identifies that dependency.

agent_checks.py combines enforcement with the captured monitoring preference. Enabled checks enforce; disabled known checks may observe; otherwise detection is off. Passive observations contain catalog identities and allowlisted numeric/boolean facts, with up to 128 retained deduplication identities. Their return value cannot authorize a blocking branch, and no model request is made by this diagnostic layer.

Capability policy controls which registered capabilities and executables are available. Permission policy evaluates execution authority. Behavior policy guides decisions and reuse. Unsafe-action policy controls dangerous operations and exact approval binding. Changing one does not imply changing all the others or granting external permissions.

Retained-answer and policy flows connect answer preservation, exact completion reevaluation, atomic scoped settings and domain-owned run recovery.

Shared authority lifecycle

native/authority_control.py owns opening, correlation, recovery and safe presentation of authority checkpoints. It makes no model calls and delegates decisions to these owners:

Kind Domain authority Effect of an accepted decision
Task resource access native/resource_access.py and the live resource-access session Bind consent to the displayed resources for this task and renew the continuation's ceiling without editing saved policies.
Legacy capability request Capability Authority and native/capability_grants.py Honor an older pending card's displayed scope, including conversation eligibility where originally requested. New issuance uses task resource access.
Permission permission_scopes.PermissionAuthority and Permission Policy Approve the exact pending operation or apply a revision-checked rule at the chosen scope.
Unsafe action execution/unsafe_authorization.py Accept one exact operation challenge with its existing volatile lifetime.
Agent Check override native/guard_strikes.py and the guard registry Change a run rule and use the guard's declared resume strategy.

The native checkpoint retains bounded authority_requests envelopes and one foreground pending_authority_request_id, with separate Activity pointers. Envelopes contain IDs, digests, scope, revisions and safe labels. Invocation arguments remain in their existing domain records. OAuth, credentials, unavailable implementations, target identity, hard safety and OS permissions remain separate.

Existing reply routes are compatibility adapters. Desktop and mobile submit the common request ID when available; supplied stale IDs are rejected. Duplicate replies cannot create a second continuation or execution. Exact permission consent survives a crash before resume starts and is retired when its pending operation is consumed. Unsafe consent remains volatile: restart, expiry or revocation cannot recreate a usable grant. Pause and Stop retain precedence over replies and admission. Existing domain events remain the Activity Trace owners, so centralization does not add duplicate cards.

Checkpoint counters record prompts opened without inference and duplicate opens; bounded process counters record rejected stale/conflicting decisions. They contain no request text or credentials and rejection counters reset when the process restarts.

Agent Introspection, Task Context, KV, Memory and Shell are always selected in Automatic and Manual capability selection. Memory tools remain available for explicit reads and writes; @use_memory enables automatic memory lookup, injection, guidance and checks for the task. The selector and capability editor do not change that automatic-support choice. It does not grant execution approval or bypass workflow restrictions, Shell executable exclusions, target prerequisites or OS permissions. Advisory mode allows local Memory and task-local KV while external Shell execution remains unavailable. Required internal tools, including all five KV tools, remain available inside workflow tool fences. This does not bypass execution permission checks.

native/unsafe_actions.py preflights concrete invocations before presenting an approval. The binding includes arguments, operation/run/request identities, authority and resolved inputs. The execution engine enforces the grant at execution. Background unsafe work cannot bypass the captured foreground path. A prior grant is not blanket authority for an unrelated command or target.

A guard rejection is a controller decision and can occur before a tool executes. An execution error records what transport/provider execution actually did. Inspect receipt metadata before assuming either means that external state is unchanged. Interrupted mutations remain unknown until the appropriate reconciliation path supplies evidence. Disabling a check does not rewrite that evidence. Redaction is an independent optional consumer projection. The retired secure-prompt guard is ignored; see Redaction.

Unsafe approval has no password field. A missing or rejected sudo value returns to the ordinary Agent loop. execution/unsafe_authorization.py retains only operation digests, receipt identities and proven non-execution facts for bounded retries; it does not store the password. The new invocation carries the literal password. The original expiry, cancellation, pause and policy revocation rules remain in force. A sequence retry preserves its completed prefix only when every prefix receipt proves success and the failed child proves that execution never started.

Unsafe-operation challenge sequence

Unsafe approval uses the same correlated authority checkpoint presentation as ordinary permission, but its usable grant is a process-local object. It is never reconstructed from a saved card. The sequence below follows native/unsafe_actions.py, memory_authority.py and UnsafeAuthority.

sequenceDiagram participant N as Native invocation owner participant E as Execution preflight participant U as Unsafe authority participant S as Native state owner participant H as Human reply route N->>E: Resolve concrete inputs and preflight each operation E-->>N: Unsafe challenge required with exact binding N->>U: Issue challenge while current policy is Ask U-->>N: Public challenge with five-minute expiry N->>S: Save pending invocation, journal and challenge identity H->>S: Submit correlated challenge decision Note over U,S: RAM acceptance holds the shared authorization lock S->>S: Recheck controls, identity, pending digest and live challenge S->>S: Publish decision or Activity input wake S->>U: Mark the original volatile record accepted after publication N->>U: Obtain still-valid private grant during owned resume N->>S: Retire saved resume opportunity before dispatch N->>E: Execute through ordinary checks and exact binding consumption

Preflight rejection keeps its original failure path; a challenge does not erase a hard denial. A shell sequence preflights all children and binds the concrete invocations together. Background/detached unsafe work does not acquire a launch intent while waiting. The binding includes capability, arguments, operation, run/request identity, target scope, resolved directory, privilege and input mode.

The RAM acceptance transaction only checks the volatile record. After successful publication, while still holding the authorization lock, it marks that same record accepted. A retried transaction therefore cannot accept twice or retain consent after rollback. Dispatch rechecks expiry and live policy. The standalone SQL path invalidates any accepted volatile challenge if its transaction fails.

Pause, Stop, changed policy, expiry or process restart prevents stale consent from executing work. Resume consumes its saved opportunity before dispatch; a crash after that point uses ordinary effect recovery. It does not create fresh approval or repeat an uncertain operation.

Narrow authentication retry

flowchart LR Result[Approved attempt returned a receipt] --> Proof{Definitely unexecuted credential-required or credential-rejected result?} Proof -->|No or effect uncertainty| Revoke[Invalidate retained challenge] Proof -->|Yes| Live{Same live accepted challenge and fewer than three retained retries?} Live -->|No| Revoke Live -->|Yes| Keep[Retain semantic digest and successful sequence-prefix receipt IDs] Keep --> Reply[Ordinary input supplies literal credential to a new invocation] Reply --> Match{Same command, scope and execution settings?} Match -->|No| Revoke Match -->|Yes| Bind[Rebind new exact operation IDs within original expiry] Bind --> Checks[Ordinary admission, safety and one-shot consumption]

The retry semantic digest omits only sudo_password and operation ID. It retains the command, target, run/request, privilege and execution settings. The authority stores digests and receipt references, never the password. A failed child can keep a completed sequence prefix only when every earlier child proves successful exit and the failed child proves no execution. Three retained authentication retries are the maximum within the original challenge lifetime; accepting a password does not extend that lifetime or waive current policy. Host-control disconnect receipts remain unverified final power state and are not replayed.

Monitoring disabled checks

Individual Agent Check switches continue to control enforcement. Fresh installations use the registry defaults: Memory inspection before work starts OFF; existing checks, including Research proof validation, execution permissions, unsafe-action checks, resource limits, and receipt verification start ON. Settings → Agent Checks → Monitor disabled Agent Checks starts ON, so disabled checks can report observations without enforcing them.

This preset is saved once when the settings database is first created. Existing installations, explicit preferences and accepted run snapshots keep their settings; an absent preference in an existing installation does not trigger the preset. The registry's inherited fallback is OFF for Memory inspection before work, which allows task work before initial memory reading and relevance assessment. When enabled, it guards that initial inspection only; memory application is best effort and never gates completion. Research proof validation defaults ON. That check controls proof requirements for research completion, including generic citation, receipt, completeness and strict response structure checks in research runs. Explicitly disabled or unavailable research proof checks are not enforced; generated answers remain available with their actual verification status. Disable all changes enforcement switches independently of monitoring.

When monitoring is ON, a disabled check can assess its native fault condition and add an informational Activity note with Learn more. The Agent continues with the established disabled-check behavior. Monitoring makes no additional model calls, opens no approval prompts, adds no model guidance, and does not change tools, routes, arguments, budgets, receipt truth or completion acceptance. Enabled checks retain their normal enforcement without passive duplicates. With monitoring OFF, disabled detectors retain their existing fast paths.

agent_checks.py owns disposition and bounded reporting; native subsystems retain their predicates. agent_check.observed is diagnostic information, not a guard strike or authority to resume/retry. The strict boolean disabled_agent_check_monitoring_enabled is captured when work is accepted. Running, queued, resumed and continued work retain that snapshot; legacy/missing values resolve OFF.

Opening plans

New actionable tasks are encouraged to show a brief Agent overview before the first tool call: the intended work, its main steps, and how the outcome will be checked. A sentence suffices for a simple task. The overview travels in the first normal decision's public content, so it requires no separate planning call. Private reasoning and tool arguments are never used as the overview. Direct answers need no preamble; explicit requests for no chat output are respected.

The overview is optional. If the first actionable decision omits it or provides only blank content, the runtime continues normal execution, including parallel actions, without a correction call or missing-plan error. This applies regardless of Agent Checks or the progress-prose toggle. Later content follows the normal progress-prose setting. A verified single-read cache recipe provides its own deterministic overview without inference.

When provided, acceptance checkpoints the overview before publishing it to the trace journal and dispatching tools. Its stable message identity prevents duplicates during replay. The Agent message stays visible after Stop, errors, refresh and restart, including when runtime issues are hidden. Ordinary waits, approvals and automatic continuations retain the existing plan or its omission; a genuine change to the user's request allows a new optional overview. Historical runs without opening-plan state need no overview. This overview does not request permission or grant execution authority.

Completion reports

New tasks require a final user-facing response by default, including tasks whose main deliverable is an action or a file. The runtime captures this requirement from the user's submission; a model declaration or compiled task cannot waive it. Disabling the optional completion check does not disable delivery of the response. The final answer itself can serve as the summary, preserving requested JSON or other exact formats without adding a second recap.

To opt out of the mandatory final response, include a standalone directive such as No chat output. or Please do not reply. in the request. Quoted text, code blocks, and examples cannot grant this opt-out. Ambiguous language keeps the default report. Approval replies and automatic continuation preserve the captured policy; a genuine change to the user's request can establish a new policy. Historical checkpoints keep their previous output contract.

When a task ends without an agent summary, including failure, Stop, or interruption, the trace journal saves a deterministic Runtime completion report with the known outcome, recorded operation counts, verification counts, and unfinished or unknown work. It makes no additional model or tool calls, does not include raw tool output, and never turns stopped or uncertain work into success. This completion message is visible even when Show runtime issues is off, and remains available after refresh and restart. Routine waits do not generate completion reports.

Productive thinking and generation quality

protocol.generation_quality detects sustained character-pattern repetition in private reasoning, extreme repetition in unfinished tool-call arguments, and inactivity in observable generation. It does not judge whether novel reasoning is useful. Reasoning, answers, tool arguments and increasing provider generation counters reset inactivity; whitespace, heartbeats and unchanged counters do not. Startup uses the configured model request timeout until the first observable generation. A provider without observable reasoning gets inactivity protection where progress is measurable, but no reasoning-loop detection. Nonstreaming responses retain their normal transport limits because intermediate generation progress is unavailable.

The repeat detector keeps raw and whitespace-normalized windows of at most 65,536 characters each per request/channel. It checks periods up to 8,192 characters, requires four copies covering at least 2,048 characters, and confirms across two checks separated by 256 new characters, independently of provider chunk boundaries. Words, punctuation and numbers are compared exactly; the fallback ignores changes in whitespace runs. This detects recurring character patterns without judging paraphrases or meaning. Tool arguments default to a higher threshold: eight copies spanning at least 16,384 characters, confirmed across the same two checks. Each tool call has independent windows, including interleaved calls. This stops runaway argument generation before the output-token limit, but can also interrupt intentionally large repetitive payloads; generate such data through compact code instead. Smaller tool-data repetitions and all repetitive answer prose remain diagnostic-only. Completed valid responses are not retroactively rejected. Activity and history receive numeric evidence and reason codes, never the detector's private text buffer.

Settings > Setup > Model routing > Tool-call repetition provides a separate switch and two thresholds: Minimum repeated characters (2,048–65,536; default 16,384) and Minimum repetitions (4–32; default 8). Both thresholds must be met. Changes are saved for the installation and apply at the next model call, including active tasks and task-contract compilation; a response already in progress keeps its captured settings. Turning this switch off leaves reasoning-loop and inactivity protection unchanged. The Generation quality check still governs enforcement; when it is disabled, enabled monitoring can record repetition without interrupting it. Neither switch changes the recovery allowance.

A repetition interruption tells the model: "You have been going in circles. Stop and rethink your approach using the existing evidence." It discards the repetitive trace and requests a fresh decision through the bounded recovery path. This does not invoke the manual stop-reasoning control or automatically disable thinking. Explicit recovery thinking settings still apply. Repetitive traces are ineligible for preserved thinking, even when generation enforcement is disabled or the response ends with a valid answer. Previously saved thinking is checked again before replay, including a loop followed by a novel conclusion.

Thinking target (%) is guidance by default. Passing the target emits one continuing notice for the pending decision; it does not discard thinking or consume output-growth attempts. Provider token limits, task resource limits and output growth remain separate. The retired automatic thinking-increase fields remain accepted by the API for compatibility. Budget state version 2 preserves the effective output allowance and pending output increase, counts that pending increase as one output attempt, and drops pending thinking-limit recovery. Migration occurs once.

Force budget and stop thinking defaults to Off in Settings beside Thinking target. On supported llama.cpp servers, an overrun offers Stop reasoning and act… on that task's status line until reasoning ends or the user clicks it. The control addresses that exact live completion while its original stream keeps running; the model can finish its answer or tool call. No partial tool call becomes executable. A failed control leaves the response running and reports the failure. Stock vLLM does not expose this manual control.

With Force budget enabled, SMTO sends a server sampling limit: reasoning_budget_tokens for llama.cpp and thinking_token_budget for vLLM. An explicit Maximum completion tokens value is required; the target is its thinking percentage rounded down, capped by any stricter configured reasoning limit. Zero closes reasoning immediately; a 100% target with no stricter cap cannot leave answer space and is reported as unavailable. Disabled thinking stays disabled. vLLM needs a compatible reasoning parser/boundary configuration (see its thinking budget documentation). Support is resolved from read-only metadata at the routed endpoint and model: llama.cpp /props?model=... sampling fields or an explicitly verified build, and vLLM's request schema. Unknown builds retain the notice and report control as unavailable. SMTO does not send test generations or control commands at startup. The llama.cpp control endpoint is called only when the user stops an eligible live response.

Toggle edits affect the next model call, including in a running task. An already dispatched response retains its policy; an output-limit continuation retains the original enforced budget and reasoning prefix so the provider counts earlier reasoning once. Soft output growth remains unchanged. Unsupported requests continue with an unavailable notice; SMTO never aborts and restarts a stream to imitate live reasoning control. Status distinguishes an accepted manual stop from a natural reasoning completion under an enabled server budget. Provider acceptance alone cannot prove that the server forced a particular transition.

A generation-quality failure schedules one retry through the existing decision loop. It retains the execution model, sampling settings, thinking configuration and effective output allowance. A second failure pauses with completed work and receipts preserved, even if malformed-response retry limits are disabled. The retry is recorded before dispatch, so restart cannot replenish it. Explicit Resume starts a new bounded episode. Cancellation, supersession and disabling the check invalidate its pending recovery. Rejected partial tool calls never execute; completed operations are not automatically replayed.

Recovery thinking's Auto and Unchanged values preserve normal settings. Explicit thinking overrides and Retry with thinking off remain opt-in and use the same single attempt. Generation inactivity timeout (llm_no_actionable_output_timeout_seconds) and Recovery inactivity timeout (llm_constrained_recovery_timeout_seconds) both default to 300 seconds and accept 30–1,800 seconds. Saved values remain unchanged and now mean inactivity allowances. Continuous progress can exceed either allowance and the soft thinking target. The optional Total recovery deadline (llm_recovery_deadline_seconds, environment AOR_LLM_RECOVERY_DEADLINE_SECONDS) defaults to 0/Off; 30–86,400 seconds imposes a total limit from dispatch, including startup. An explicit total deadline applies even with the check off. Rejected-stream cleanup remains separately bounded to at most 30 seconds. Task Contract and capability-selection limits retain their own policies.

These changes do not enable checks or replace existing scoped preferences. Observe-only monitoring reports the same conservative signal without rejecting generation or scheduling recovery. Compare observation and enforcement using an offline replay with tool dispatch disabled before enabling enforcement for a provider.
